newsitem.title: USA: B.A.T gets approval to sell 6 U.S. brands.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T gets approval to sell 6 U.S. brands.

text.p: Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, said on Friday that the U.S. Federal Trade Commission approved the company's agreement to sell six former American Tobacco cigarette brands to Commonwealth Tobacco LLC.
Sale of the brands was part of a consent order issued by the agency in December 1994 after B.A.T Industries acquired the American Tobacco Co, the company said.
With the FTC's aproval, Bown & Williamson will formally close the sale with Commonwealth.
The sale includes domestic rights to Montclair, Malibu, Riviera, Crowns, Special 10's and Bull Durham cigarettes.
Also, Commonwealth will acquire a cigarette manufacturing plant that was formerly owned by American Tobacco in Reidsville, N.C.

In Washington, the FTC confirmed the 5-to-0 decision, noting it had rejected B.A.T's earlier application to sell the assets to Lorillard Tobacco Co on April 10 due to concern that Lorillard would not compete aggressively in the discount cigarette market.

But it said it had determined "that divestiture to Commonwealth will accomplish the order's purposes by transferring the assets to a firm with the incentive and the ability to compete in the discount segment of the market."
